newsitem.title: ESTONIA: FARMA GETS REDUCED RUSSIAN CUSTOMS RATE.
newsitem.headline: FARMA GETS REDUCED RUSSIAN CUSTOMS RATE.

text.p: Tallinna Farma pharmaceutical plant said on Tuesday that it has reached an agreement to reduce the customs on its imports to Russia from June.

In a statement the company said that the Russian customs service has given it the right to receive raw materials from Russia, exempting the company from customs duty when the materials are used in products imported to Russia.
Instead of the current 20 percent import duties the company will have to pay an administrative fee of 0.15 percent on the value of the goods imported into Russia.
The exemption will only be granted if Tallinna Farma receives orders from Russia to manufacture the drugs.
One Russia's largest medical companies, FIRN-M, will handle the sales and orders for Tallinna Farma.
The Russian health ministry has issued a certificate to FIRN-M saying that Tallinn Farma has the right to manufacture drugs as a service for FIRN-M.
